title: EVALUATE without WHEN OTHER silently skips on unmatched value
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. POLICY-DISCOUNT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-AGE-BAND        PIC X.
       01  WS-DISCOUNT-PCT    PIC 9(2)V99.
      *> Missing WHEN OTHER: any WS-AGE-BAND value not in {Y, M, S}
      *> leaves WS-DISCOUNT-PCT at its prior value -- the EVALUATE
      *> falls through silently. Real production bugs from this
      *> pattern: a typo'd input ('y' lowercase) silently inherits
      *> the previous record's discount.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       SET-DISCOUNT.
           EVALUATE WS-AGE-BAND
              WHEN "Y"
                 MOVE 5.00  TO WS-DISCOUNT-PCT
              WHEN "M"
                 MOVE 10.00 TO WS-DISCOUNT-PCT
              WHEN "S"
                 MOVE 15.00 TO WS-DISCOUNT-PCT
           END-EVALUATE.
notes:
Missing-WHEN-OTHER is one of the most common COBOL silent-bug
patterns surfaced in migration audits. A modernised rewrite with
an exhaustive switch / sealed sum-type would force the engineer
to handle the default branch -- which is *exactly* the behaviour
change the customer doesn't want without an explicit SME sign-off.
The extract must flag the fall-through semantic AND surface the
'what should happen on unmatched input?' question for the SME.
